###  Establishing your identity
We need to establish your identity before discussing or updating your tax record or one you're authorised for. We'll ask you questions based on information we hold about you, including information from third parties and other government departments. This may include:
  * details from letters or notices we have issued to you
  * information you have provided us such as details from a tax return
  * details from accounts you hold with us such as payment or refund amounts
  * information related to your interactions with us
  * details of your employment, superannuation or investments you hold.


We may also ask to confirm details of identity documents such as your driver licence, Medicare card or passport.
We recommend you have your tax file number (TFN) or Australian business number (ABN) ready when you phone us.
To save time, we recommend you use [voice authentication](https://www.ato.gov.au/online-services/voice-authentication) for a fast and secure way to verify your identity over the phone. When you phone us, ask to enrol your unique voiceprint. If you enrol, you can then use your voice to verify your identity for future calls.

####  Business enquiries
For business enquiries, phone [13 28 66External Link](tel:132866) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday to discuss:
  * account balances
  * business registrations
  * business tax return preparation
  * business activity statements
  * Single Touch Payroll
  * excise and fuel schemes or grants
  * foreign resident capital gains withholding
  * global and domestic minimum tax.


####  Call services for hearing or speech/communication difficulties
If you are d/Deaf, hard of hearing or have a speech/communication difficulty you can contact us through the [National Relay ServiceExternal Link](https://www.accesshub.gov.au/about-the-nrs) (NRS), as follows:
  1. Contact the NRS through your preferred NRS call channel, detailed in [NRS call numbers and linksExternal Link](https://www.accesshub.gov.au/about-the-nrs/nrs-call-numbers-and-links) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
  2. Provide the NRS with the ATO phone number you want to call.


####  Call back lines
You can only use these call back numbers if someone from the ATO contacted you by phone, SMS or letter and asked you to phone us back. Be aware that if we phone you, you won't see a number on caller ID.
If you receive a call claiming to be from the ATO you can use the [Verify a call feature](https://www.ato.gov.au/online-services/online-services-for-individuals-and-sole-traders/ato-app/manage-your-tax-and-super-with-the-ato-app#verifycall) in the ATO app to verify that the call is genuinely from us.
##### Compliance activity call-back line
Phone us back on the Compliance activity call-back line on [1300 650 286External Link](tel:1300650286) between 8:00 am to 5:00 pm Monday to Friday.
The ATO staff member will give you a PIN that you must enter when prompted. This will ensure you are directed to the right customer service representative.
##### Lodgment support call-back line
Phone us back on the Lodgment support call-back line on [1300 661 508External Link](tel:1300661508) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
For general enquiries use our [Lodge and Pay enquiries line](https://www.ato.gov.au/about-ato/contact-us#LodgeandPayenquiries).
##### Payment support call-back line
Phone us back on the Payment support call-back line on [1300 880 217External Link](tel:1300880217) or [1300 466 859External Link](tel:1300466859) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
For general enquiries use our [Lodge and Pay enquiries line](https://www.ato.gov.au/about-ato/contact-us#LodgeandPayenquiries).
####  Emergency support line
For assistance due to a [crisis or disaster](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/financial-difficulties-and-disasters), phone our Emergency support line on [1800 806 218External Link](tel:1800806218) between

8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
####  Foreign investment enquiries
Before phoning us, see information about how to [contact us about foreign investment](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/foreign-resident-investments/foreign-investment-in-australia/contact-us-about-foreign-investment).
For foreign investment enquiries, phone [1800 050 377External Link](tel:1800050377) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
####  Identity theft
If you think your TFN has been stolen or misused, phone [1800 467 033External Link](tel:1800467033) 8:00 am to 6:00 pm (AEST) Monday to Friday.
For more information, see [Help for identity theft](https://www.ato.gov.au/online-services/scams-cyber-safety-and-identity-protection/help-for-identity-theft).
####  Indigenous Helpline
The Indigenous Helpline is a specialist service for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. Phone [13 10 30External Link](tel:131030) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
Our Indigenous Helpline staff specialise in supporting Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples with things like getting a tax file number, lodging a tax return, or finding your super.
####  Individual enquiries
For individual enquiries, phone [13 28 61External Link](tel:132861) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday to discuss:
  * myTax
  * tax file number
  * progress of returns (self-help option only)
  * tax return preparation
  * higher education or trade loans
  * PAYG instalments for individuals
  * support linking the ATO to myGov.


####  International GST enquiries
For International GST enquiries, phone [+61 2 6216 1111External Link](tel:+61262161111) between 8:00 am to 5:00 pm (AEST) Monday to Friday, then ask the operator to connect you to [1300 146 094External Link](tel:1300146094) Fast Key Code **1 1 8**. You will be transferred to an officer who can help you.
You can also phone the [Translating and Interpreting Service](https://www.ato.gov.au/about-ato/contact-us#Translatingandinterpretingservice) and ask to be connected to [1300 146 094External Link](tel:1300146094).
####  Lodge and pay enquiries
For lodge and pay enquiries, phone [13 11 42External Link](tel:131142) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday to discuss:
  * new and existing debts
  * payment plans
  * overdue lodgments
  * penalties and interest.


####  Not-for-profit organisation enquiries
For not-for-profit organisation enquiries, phone [1300 130 248External Link](tel:1300130248) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday to discuss:
  * registrations
  * DGR endorsement
  * reporting
  * updating your organisations details.


####  Overseas enquiries
##### Linking the ATO to myGov
If you need support linking the ATO to your myGov account and you are ringing from outside Australia, phone [+61 2 6216 3444External Link](tel:+61262163444) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
##### General
If you are ringing from outside Australia and you are comfortable speaking English, phone [+61 2 6216 1111External Link](tel:+61262161111) between 8:00 am to 5:00 pm (AEST) Monday to Friday.
If you prefer to speak with us in a language other than English, you can phone the Translating and Interpreting Service (TIS National) on [+61 3 9268 8332External Link](tel:+61392688332) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
This free service provides an interpreter in one of these [available languagesExternal Link](https://www.tisnational.gov.au/Who-we-are/We-speak-your-language). The service will connect you and an interpreter to us so we can help with your query.

rag_samples.question: Compare ATO fin.-difficulty/disaster support with its info-accuracy commitment: help offered vs stated assurances.
rag_samples.reference:
The ATO offers practical help for people facing **financial difficulties and disasters**, including a dedicated **Help and support** area and contact options for tailored assistance.

Its **information-accuracy commitment** is a separate assurance: the ATO says it aims to provide **accurate, consistent and clear information** to help people understand their rights and obligations. It also states that if you rely on ATO information and it is **incorrect or misleading**, and this causes a mistake, the ATO will **take that into account** when deciding what action to take.

In short:
- **Help offered:** support pathways for people experiencing financial hardship or disasters.
- **Stated assurances:** a commitment to clear, reliable information, with consideration given if ATO information was wrong or misleading.

rag_samples.question: Which disability-related tax offsets, GST car concessions, tax-free payments, and super rules apply?
rag_samples.reference:
If you have a disability, you or your carer may be eligible for:

- **Tax offsets or rebates** to help reduce the tax you pay  
- **GST concessions on cars**, including when you **buy or lease a car** or **buy car parts**  
- **Tax-free government pensions and payments** if you’re a person with disability or care for someone with disability  
- **Superannuation rules and access options** specifically for people with disability  
- **Invalidity or disability payments** from your employer or super fund if you can no longer work due to disability  
- **NDIS-related tax information**, including **payments, deductions and tax** for participants in the National Disability Insurance Scheme

You can find these under the ATO’s **People with disability** information, including:
- **Tax offsets for people with disability**
- **Tax concessions on cars for people with disability**
- **Government pensions and payments for people with disability**
- **Superannuation for people with disability**
- **Invalidity or disability payments from employers or super funds**
- **National disability insurance scheme**

rag_samples.question: Compare Norfolk Island tax & super obligations for individuals, businesses, NFPs, and employers.
rag_samples.reference:
Norfolk Island tax and super obligations differ by group:

- **Individuals:** Information covers paying tax, applying for a TFN, lodging a tax return, and claiming income and deductions.
- **Businesses:** Must consider tax, reporting, and record-keeping requirements.
- **Not-for-profits (NFPs):** Have dedicated tax information specific to NFP organisations on Norfolk Island.
- **Employers:** Need to meet **super obligations** for their employees.

The ATO also provides separate guidance on:
- **Norfolk Island tax and super** generally, explaining how Australian tax and super laws apply
- **Super for individuals**, including contributions, tracking super, and how benefits are paid

### Our commitment to you
We are committed to providing you with accurate, consistent and clear information to help you understand your rights and entitlements and meet your obligations.
If you follow our information and it turns out to be incorrect, or it is misleading and you make a mistake as a result, we will take that into account when determining what action, if any, we should take.

rag_samples.reference:
ATO login portals listed in the context are:

- **Sole traders / individuals** – sign in to **myGov** via ATO online services for individuals  
- **BAS agents / registered tax agents** – **Agents** online services login  
- **Non-resident GST importers** – **Non-residents** login via **AusID**  
- **Foreign investors** – **Foreign investor** online services login

rag_samples.question: From ATO content, list 6 online services and quote “Our commitment to you” accuracy pledge.
rag_samples.reference:
Six ATO online services listed are:

1. **Individuals** – access ATO online and complete your tax return via myTax through myGov  
2. **Business** – interact online for business tax and super needs  
3. **Agents** – for registered tax and BAS agents and authorised staff  
4. **Non-residents** – register, report and pay GST in Australia via AusID  
5. **Access manager** – manage who has electronic access to a business’s tax information  
6. **Foreign investor** – report and manage Australian asset registrations and related obligations  

**“Our commitment to you” accuracy pledge:**  
“We are committed to providing you with accurate, consistent and clear information to help you understand your rights and entitlements and meet your obligations.”

If the information **doesn’t fully cover your circumstances** or you’re **unsure how it applies**, the ATO advises you to **contact them or seek professional advice**.

rag_samples.question: For individual enquiries, give the phone no. and hrs, plus list 2 supported topics.
rag_samples.reference:
For individual enquiries, call **13 28 61** between **8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday**.

Two supported topics are:
- **myTax**
- **tax file number**
relevant_contexts:
8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
####  Foreign investment enquiries
Before phoning us, see information about how to [contact us about foreign investment](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/investments-and-assets/foreign-resident-investments/foreign-investment-in-australia/contact-us-about-foreign-investment).
For foreign investment enquiries, phone [1800 050 377External Link](tel:1800050377) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
####  Identity theft
If you think your TFN has been stolen or misused, phone [1800 467 033External Link](tel:1800467033) 8:00 am to 6:00 pm (AEST) Monday to Friday.
For more information, see [Help for identity theft](https://www.ato.gov.au/online-services/scams-cyber-safety-and-identity-protection/help-for-identity-theft).
####  Indigenous Helpline
The Indigenous Helpline is a specialist service for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. Phone [13 10 30External Link](tel:131030) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
Our Indigenous Helpline staff specialise in supporting Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples with things like getting a tax file number, lodging a tax return, or finding your super.
####  Individual enquiries
For individual enquiries, phone [13 28 61External Link](tel:132861) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday to discuss:
  * myTax
  * tax file number
  * progress of returns (self-help option only)
  * tax return preparation
  * higher education or trade loans
  * PAYG instalments for individuals
  * support linking the ATO to myGov.


####  International GST enquiries
For International GST enquiries, phone [+61 2 6216 1111External Link](tel:+61262161111) between 8:00 am to 5:00 pm (AEST) Monday to Friday, then ask the operator to connect you to [1300 146 094External Link](tel:1300146094) Fast Key Code **1 1 8**. You will be transferred to an officer who can help you.
You can also phone the [Translating and Interpreting Service](https://www.ato.gov.au/about-ato/contact-us#Translatingandinterpretingservice) and ask to be connected to [1300 146 094External Link](tel:1300146094).
####  Lodge and pay enquiries
For lodge and pay enquiries, phone [13 11 42External Link](tel:131142) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday to discuss:
  * new and existing debts
  * payment plans
  * overdue lodgments
  * penalties and interest.


####  Not-for-profit organisation enquiries
For not-for-profit organisation enquiries, phone [1300 130 248External Link](tel:1300130248) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday to discuss:
  * registrations
  * DGR endorsement
  * reporting
  * updating your organisations details.


####  Overseas enquiries
##### Linking the ATO to myGov
If you need support linking the ATO to your myGov account and you are ringing from outside Australia, phone [+61 2 6216 3444External Link](tel:+61262163444) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
##### General
If you are ringing from outside Australia and you are comfortable speaking English, phone [+61 2 6216 1111External Link](tel:+61262161111) between 8:00 am to 5:00 pm (AEST) Monday to Friday.
If you prefer to speak with us in a language other than English, you can phone the Translating and Interpreting Service (TIS National) on [+61 3 9268 8332External Link](tel:+61392688332) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
This free service provides an interpreter in one of these [available languagesExternal Link](https://www.tisnational.gov.au/Who-we-are/We-speak-your-language). The service will connect you and an interpreter to us so we can help with your query. 
We provide a range of [Information in other languages](https://www.ato.gov.au/other-languages).

  * excise and fuel schemes or grants
  * foreign resident capital gains withholding
  * global and domestic minimum tax.


####  Call services for hearing or speech/communication difficulties
If you are d/Deaf, hard of hearing or have a speech/communication difficulty you can contact us through the [National Relay ServiceExternal Link](https://www.accesshub.gov.au/about-the-nrs) (NRS), as follows:
  1. Contact the NRS through your preferred NRS call channel, detailed in [NRS call numbers and linksExternal Link](https://www.accesshub.gov.au/about-the-nrs/nrs-call-numbers-and-links) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
  2. Provide the NRS with the ATO phone number you want to call.


####  Call back lines
You can only use these call back numbers if someone from the ATO contacted you by phone, SMS or letter and asked you to phone us back. Be aware that if we phone you, you won't see a number on caller ID.
If you receive a call claiming to be from the ATO you can use the [Verify a call feature](https://www.ato.gov.au/online-services/online-services-for-individuals-and-sole-traders/ato-app/manage-your-tax-and-super-with-the-ato-app#verifycall) in the ATO app to verify that the call is genuinely from us.
##### Compliance activity call-back line
Phone us back on the Compliance activity call-back line on [1300 650 286External Link](tel:1300650286) between 8:00 am to 5:00 pm Monday to Friday.
The ATO staff member will give you a PIN that you must enter when prompted. This will ensure you are directed to the right customer service representative.
##### Lodgment support call-back line
Phone us back on the Lodgment support call-back line on [1300 661 508External Link](tel:1300661508) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
For general enquiries use our [Lodge and Pay enquiries line](https://www.ato.gov.au/about-ato/contact-us#LodgeandPayenquiries).
##### Payment support call-back line
Phone us back on the Payment support call-back line on [1300 880 217External Link](tel:1300880217) or [1300 466 859External Link](tel:1300466859) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
For general enquiries use our [Lodge and Pay enquiries line](https://www.ato.gov.au/about-ato/contact-us#LodgeandPayenquiries).
####  Emergency support line
For assistance due to a [crisis or disaster](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/financial-difficulties-and-disasters), phone our Emergency support line on [1800 806 218External Link](tel:1800806218) between

####  Registered tax professionals
Registered tax professionals can phone [13 72 86External Link](tel:137286) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
For more information, see [Phone services for tax professionals](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-and-super-professionals/for-tax-professionals/support-and-communication/phone-services).
####  SBR Software service
To [Notify us of a hosted SBR software service](https://www.ato.gov.au/online-services/access-manager/about-access-manager) phone [1300 852 232External Link](tel:1300852232) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
####  Scam reporting
To report a scam, phone [1800 008 540External Link](tel:1800008540) between 8:00 am to 6:00 pm Monday to Friday.
If you receive a call claiming to be from the ATO you can use the [Verify a call feature](https://www.ato.gov.au/online-services/online-services-for-individuals-and-sole-traders/ato-app/manage-your-tax-and-super-with-the-ato-app#verifycall) in the ATO app to verify that the call is genuinely from us.

rag_samples.question: Compare ATO support for personal crisis, natural disasters, COVID-19, agencies, mental health, and finance advice.
rag_samples.reference:
ATO support covers several areas:

- **Personal crisis or financial hardship**: Help for people experiencing physical or mental health issues, domestic violence, financial hardship, or death.
- **Natural disaster support**: Support after events like bushfires, cyclones, droughts, earthquakes, floods, landslides, or storms.
- **COVID-19 tax support**: Tailored tax support made available due to COVID-19.
- **Support from other agencies**: Information on accessing payments, grants, and other help outside the ATO.
- **Mental health, wellbeing and counselling services**: Links to support services if you’re feeling overwhelmed.
- **Advice on managing your finances**: The ATO doesn’t provide financial advice, but points you to other organisations and websites for financial tips and counselling.

In short, ATO support ranges from direct tax and hardship assistance to referrals for wellbeing, grants, and financial counselling.

rag_samples.question: Outline rare NI tax/super edge cases for residents, NFPs, sole traders, and employers.
rag_samples.reference:
Rare Norfolk Island tax and super edge cases can include:

- **Residents:** unusual situations around **TFN applications, lodging tax returns, and claiming specific income or deductions**, especially where residency or income sources are not straightforward. The ATO points residents to guidance on **paying tax, applying for a TFN, lodging a return, income and deductions**.
- **Not-for-profit organisations:** edge cases about whether an organisation’s activities affect its **tax treatment or obligations**, covered under the ATO’s **Not-for-profit organisations** guidance for Norfolk Island.
- **Sole traders / businesses:** uncommon issues with **tax, reporting and record-keeping requirements**, particularly where the business structure or transactions are unusual. The ATO directs Norfolk Island businesses to its **Tax for businesses** information.
- **Employers:** special cases involving **super obligations**, including when and how super contributions must be made for workers on Norfolk Island. The ATO provides this under **Super for employers**.
- **Individuals and super:** less common matters about **super entitlements, tracking super, and payment of benefits**, covered under **Super for individuals**.

For detailed rules, the ATO’s Norfolk Island sections are:
**Norfolk Island tax and super**, **Norfolk Island residents and individual tax**, **Tax for businesses**, **Not-for-profit organisations**, **Super for individuals**, and **Super for employers**.

rag_samples.question: Examine blockchain‑based record‑keeping for gig‑economy tax deduction claims in AUS.
rag_samples.reference:
Blockchain‑based record‑keeping could streamline gig‑economy tax deduction claims in Australia by providing an immutable, time‑stamped ledger of income and expenses. However, the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) still requires that records be:

* **Verifiable and accessible** – the ATO must be able to review the evidence, so blockchain entries must be exportable in a format the ATO accepts (e.g., PDF, CSV, or a trusted audit trail).
* **Retained for five years** – records must be kept for the period specified in the ATO’s “Records you need to keep” guide.
* **Relevant to the claim** – only income, deductions, and offsets that the ATO recognises (as outlined in the “Guides for occupations and industries”) can be claimed.

Using blockchain can satisfy these conditions if the system is designed to produce compliant, auditable records. It offers a secure way to prove gig‑economy earnings and expenses, but the data must still meet the ATO’s format and retention requirements.

rag_samples.question: Detail steps for reporting crypto‑asset capital gains in Australian tax returns.
rag_samples.reference:
**How to report crypto‑asset capital gains in your Australian tax return**

1. **Track every transaction**  
   * Record the date, amount, and price (in AUD) of each purchase, sale, or exchange of crypto‑assets.  
   * Keep receipts, bank statements, or exchange records as evidence.

2. **Calculate the capital gain or loss**  
   * **Capital gain** = sale proceeds – cost base (purchase price + any incidental costs).  
   * **Capital loss** = cost base – sale proceeds.  
   * If you hold the asset for 12 months or more, you may be eligible for the 50 % CGT discount on the gain.

3. **Net the gains and losses**  
   * Add all capital gains and subtract all capital losses to arrive at a net capital gain (or loss) for the financial year.

4. **Include the net amount in your tax return**  
   * Report the net capital gain on the **Capital Gains** section of the individual tax return (Form 1040‑A or the online ATO portal).  
   * If you have a net loss, you can carry it forward to offset future gains.

5. **Declare the income**  
   * Crypto‑asset capital gains are considered **investment income** and must be declared in the tax return.  
   * They are taxable, assessable, and subject to the same CGT rules as other investment assets.

6. **Use ATO resources**  
   * Refer to the ATO’s “Taxable assessable and exempt income” guidance for detailed rules on capital gains.  
   * If you’re unsure about the CGT discount or how to calculate the cost base, consult the ATO’s “Business, partnership and trust income” page for additional examples.

By following these steps, you’ll correctly report crypto‑asset capital gains and comply with Australian tax law.

rag_samples.question: Suppose you earned $5k interest & $2k dividends from investments; how claim deductions?
rag_samples.reference:
You can claim the costs that were incurred to earn that $5 000 interest and $2 000 dividend income.

1. **Gather records** – keep receipts or statements that show the interest‑earning expenses (e.g., loan interest, investment account fees) and any related costs for the dividends (e.g., brokerage fees).

2. **Claim on your tax return** – on the *Deductions* section of your individual tax return, enter the total deductible amount for:
   * **Interest income** – the costs that earned the $5 000 interest.
   * **Dividend income** – the costs that earned the $2 000 dividend.

3. **Use the ATO guidance** – the ATO page on *Interest, dividend and other investment income deductions* explains the types of expenses that are deductible and how to calculate the amount:  
   <https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/income-deductions-offsets-and-records/deductions-you-can-claim/investments-insurance-and-super/interest-dividend-and-other-investment-income-deductions>

4. **Other related deductions** – if you also paid insurance premiums to protect employment income or made personal super contributions, those can be claimed on the same return (see the same ATO page for details).

Simply report the deductible amounts on your tax return, and the ATO will reduce your taxable income accordingly.

rag_samples.question: Detail TFN application for overseas contractors.
rag_samples.reference:
**Applying for a TFN as an overseas contractor**

1. **Who needs a TFN?**  
   • Any person who receives Australian income (e.g., contractor payments) must have a TFN.  
   • Non‑residents can still apply; the TFN is required for tax‑withholding and reporting.

2. **How to apply**  
   • **Online** – Use the ATO’s *TFN application* portal (https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/tax-file-number/).  
   • **Paper** – Download the *TFN application form* (Form 6055) from the same page, fill it out, and mail it to the ATO.  
   • **Through a tax agent** – If you’re working with a registered agent, they can submit on your behalf.

3. **Documents you’ll need**  
   • Valid passport (or other government ID).  
   • Proof of overseas address (utility bill, bank statement, etc.).  
   • If you’re a company or trust, include the relevant entity documents.

4. **Processing time**  
   • Online applications are usually processed within 2–3 business days.  
   • Paper applications may take up to 4 weeks.

5. **After you receive your TFN**  
   • Provide it to your Australian client so they can withhold the correct tax.  
   • Keep the TFN confidential; report any loss or theft immediately (see ATO guidance).

6. **Residency note**  
   • If you’re coming to Australia or staying long‑term, your residency status may change your tax obligations. Review the *Coming to Australia or going overseas* page for details.

**Quick links**  
- TFN application portal: https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/tax-file-number/  
- TFN application form (PDF): https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/tax-file-number/Apply-for-a-TFN/  

Follow these steps to obtain your TFN and comply with Australian tax requirements as an overseas contractor.
